en.title: 🔥 No modeling, no artists: one person used AI to build a full-fledged 3D action game that's genuinely playable—and released the full prompt set, from single-image rigging to a two-platform playable demo
en.summary: AI-generated 3D characters look cool—until they start moving, clipping through themselves, sliding around, or failing to grip a weapon. Using a Three Kingdoms action game, Fini breaks down the full pipeline from a single reference image to a title playable on both PC and mobile: standardizing character art, generating models and animations, compressing assets, then fixing animation details step by step while adding combat impact and boss fights.

LLM is everything: Why was ByteDance the first to serve up a Personal Agent?

Tried ByteDance's newly launched Xiaodou today—the level of polish is higher than expected.
Why was it ByteDance, not Alibaba or Tencent, that first got a Personal Agent out the door?

Tencent clearly holds the better hand: social relationship chains, user stickiness, and the earliest nationwide rollout of the Workbuddy base.

Because LLM is everything.
Model capability is the foundational bedrock of all AI business.

Ordinary people's personal needs are too scattered and too long-tail—engineers simply can't enumerate them all.
Only when the base model is strong enough does the Agent no longer need so much fine-tuning.
No need to hand-hold it through which button to click first, what to look up second.

en.title: Chatting in a group: for those running AI media accounts, how do you usually find story angles?
en.summary:
Got to talking in a group chat: for those of you doing AI content creation, how do you usually find topic angles?

Let me start with my own situation 👇
I just passed 12,000 followers on Xiaohongshu doing AI content — not explosive growth, and no viral posts with tens of thousands of likes.

But every post performs consistently, and monetization has been running smoothly:

1️⃣ Landed my first sponsored deal with a top model company at 1,000+ followers; from 4,000+ followers I've had back-to-back brand deals every month; at 8,000+ I signed with an MCN (deal referrals only, no content support)
2️⃣ Now I get dozens of collaboration inquiries every month, with a wide range of products (LLMs, office Agents, AIGC, hardware) and solid rates.
3️⃣ Since I have a day job, I take at most three or four a month, and my rates have been climbing over the past few months.

Many people assume brand deals come down to follower count. I think when brands put real money behind a budget, they care more about two things:

- Whether the content has a natural "ad slot…
en.reason: A Xiaohongshu AI creator with just over 12,000 followers recounts landing a first top model-brand deal at 1,000+ followers, monthly deals from 4,000+, an MCN signing at 8,000+, and dozens of monthly invitations, accepting three or four.

LLM is everything: Why was ByteDance the first to serve up a Personal Agent?

Tried ByteDance's newly launched Xiaodou today—the level of polish is higher than expected.
Why was it ByteDance, not Alibaba or Tencent, that first got a Personal Agent out the door?

When it comes to closing the loop between goods and transactions, Alibaba is the ceiling.
Tencent clearly holds the better hand: social relationship chains, user stickiness, and the earliest nationwide rollout of the Workbuddy base.

Because LLM is everything.
Model capability is the foundational bedrock of all AI business.

Ordinary people's personal needs are too scattered and too long-tail—engineers simply can't enumerate them all.
Only when the base model is strong enough does the Agent no longer need so much fine-tuning.
No need to hand-hold it through which button to click first, what to look up second.

en.summary:
Got to talking in a group chat: for those of you doing AI content creation, how do you usually find topic angles?

But every post performs consistently, and monetization has been running smoothly:

1️⃣ Landed my first sponsored deal with a top model company at 1,000+ followers; from 4,000+ followers I've had back-to-back brand deals every month; at 8,000+ I signed with an MCN (deal referrals only, no content support)
2️⃣ Now I get dozens of collaboration inquiries every month, with a wide range of products (LLMs, office Agents, AIGC, hardware) and solid rates.
3️⃣ Since I have a day job, I take at most three or four a month, and my rates have been climbing over the past few months.

- Whether the content has a natural "ad slot…
